title: Just Another Small Channel Stuck in View Jail, and Then...
one_sentence_summary: By shifting from simply recounting history to structuring videos around strong hooks and a repeatable three-act narrative template driven by curiosity gaps, a creator broke out of view jail to achieve over 100,000 views per video.
key_takeaways: Stop starting videos with generic self-introductions; instead, open with a compelling hook, a story, and a clear reason for the viewer to care within the first 10 seconds.
Formulate an overarching curiosity gap by constantly asking 'what am I genuinely curious about and what happens if I pull the thread?'.
Apply a three-act structure to your video scripts, ensuring sections systematically raise a question, complicate what viewers think they know, and deliver an insightful answer.
Use comment or highlight features in your scriptwriting to label major beats, catalysts, and climaxes to maintain a tight narrative flow.
Fix the core idea and question before spending hours on execution and polish, as a good video cannot rescue a bad underlying concept.

actionable_frameworks.name: The Three-Act Video Template
actionable_frameworks.description: A structural storytelling method where every section raises a question, complicates it by challenging assumptions, and finally answers it to maintain high viewer engagement.

actionable_frameworks.name: The Curiosity Gap Framework
actionable_frameworks.description: A narrative approach that shifts content creation from simple recounting of history to exploring a compelling core question that drives the viewer to stick around for the answer.

memorable_quotes: A good video cannot rescue a bad idea.
Stop recounting history and start asking what am I genuinely curious about and what happens if I pull the thread?
